{{Quote|Your generic TIE grunt is just plain suicidal. And the TIE Defender jockey is bloodthirsty. But the TIE Interceptor pilot, he's suicidal ''and'' bloodthirsty. When you see a squad of those maniacs flying your way, you'd better hope your hyperdrive is operational.|[[Kyle Katarn]]|<ref name="NEGVV" />}}
The '''TIE/IN starfighter''', simply known as the '''TIE Interceptor''', '''T/I'''<ref name="Star Wars: Tie Fighter">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref> or '''SFS-TIE/I/1''',<ref name="XvT">''[[Starfighter Battle Book: X-wing vs TIE Interceptor]]''</ref> was a [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The TIE [[Interceptor/Legends|Interceptor]] was identifiable by its arrow-shaped [[solar gather-panel|solar collection panels]], a distinct difference from the hexagonal solar arrays of its predecessor, the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN Fighter]]. The Interceptor was one of the fastest [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at its prime, nearly rivaling the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance's]] [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]].

Due to their speed, distinct shape, and narrow profile in comparison to the TIE/LN starfighter (which was nicknamed "[[List of phrases and slang/Legends|eyeball]]"), TIE Interceptors came to be referred to occasionally as "squints" by enemy pilots.<ref name="Alliance Intelligence Report: TIE Fighters">{{JournalCite|10|Alliance Intelligence Report: TIE Fighters}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:TIE_Interceptor_by_Darren_Tan.jpg|thumb|left|180px|TIE/IN interceptor]]
Like most TIE models, the TIE Interceptor shared nearly identical cockpits, drive pods, and wing brace designs with the TIE Fighter. The solar collector panels were lengthened and angled, and the forward center section was removed. This new solar array design gave the Interceptor its unmistakable dagger-like appearance and shrinking its profile to make targeting more frustrating for enemy [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> This wing design gave the craft a more menacing visage, continuing the Empire's reputation of ruling through fear.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The original production model came equipped with either four identical [[Senko Systems]] [[80-100 laser cannon|80-100 laser cannons]] with a fire control system that allowed only diagonally opposite guns to fire at the same time to facilitate rapid heat dissipation,<ref name="XvsTIE" /> or four [[L-s9.3 laser cannon/Legends|L-s9.3 laser cannons]] with each weapon able to fire either on its own or linked to the other three. Both types of crafts had one cannon installed on each wingtip. New targeting software was installed in the TIE Interceptor, and the [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|SFS]] [[T-s9a targeting computer/Legends|T-s9a targeting computer]] offered greater accuracy during complex flight maneuvers.<ref name="TSC" /> While the models equipped with Senko Systems' weaponry had them replaced with [[Sensor/Legends|sensor receptors]],<ref name="XvsTIE" /> twin [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] hardpoints still remained on the "chin" portion of the other model's cockpit module. Provided that technicians could find room for additional power generators, these cannons could also be utilized.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" /> Further upgrades, including [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] and advanced shielding made them equal to the Rebellion's [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] starfighters.<ref name="SW 4 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 4|''Star Wars'' (2013) 4]]</ref> Their weapons were equipped with safeties.<ref name="SW 11 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 11|''Star Wars'' (2013) 11]]</ref>

Later TIE Interceptor models were modified to carry four [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]], replacing the original wingtip laser cannons. The twin chin-mounted laser cannons remained. The new model also came equipped with multi-purpose warhead launchers. These upgrades made the new model more of a multi-purpose fighter rather than an Interceptor, though it still retained its original name. However, despite the adoption of a new model, the older model remained a common sight in Imperial fleets for years to come.<ref name="NEGVV" />

<div style="float:right">[[File:Fightercover.png|thumb|left|180px|A TIE Interceptor firing its "chin" [[Laser cannon/Legends|cannons]].]]</div>
The TIE Interceptor fielded [[P-s5.6 twin ion engine/Legends|P-s5.6 twin ion engines]].<ref name="TSC" /> The new engines included an advanced ion-stream projector, thus allowing pilots access to more sophisticated combat maneuvers. Twin-port deflectors supported this feat by allowing the pilot individual manipulation of the deflectors, thus providing finer flight control.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" /> These advancements in engine technology made the TIE Interceptor a superior platform in space combat, achieving speeds beyond all other Alliance starfighters short of the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]].<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> Interceptors assigned to [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Kell Bircher]]'s elite squadron were also equipped with [[Afterburner/Legends|afterburners]].<ref name="SW 11 (DH)" />

The TIE Interceptor's primary role was as its title suggested. Like its predecessors, the Interceptor lacked heavier armor, [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], and [[Life support/Legends|life support]] systems (though shields and a small hyperdrive could be fitted as an upgrade, these were uncommon). Interceptor pilots were forced to rely on speed, maneuverability, superior numbers, and advanced weapon systems to prevail in its primary role of space superiority.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" /> The craft's drawbacks meant that any pilot who survived more than a few missions was considered to be a "top gun" in the Imperial fleet.<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

With no hyperdrive, the TIE Interceptor was reliant on a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] for an operations base. [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and prominent [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] such as [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] and [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]] were common staging areas for Interceptor squadrons; however, smaller vessels and more remote locations had to rely on aging [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" />

[[File:Pincer5.jpg|thumb|left|180px|TIE Interceptors engaging the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].]]
There was also a [[Emperor's Royal Guard TIE/IN starfighter|special variant]], painted completely red with significant upgrades, that was available for use by the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Emperor's Royal Guards]]. Aside from its paint job and upgrades, this model also featured two small wings protruding from each solar panel.<ref name="Star Wars: Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

TIE Interceptors had powerful solar ionization reactors, the same model used in the [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE Avenger]]. These could handle the special equipment built into the Interceptor, including deflector shields, beam weapons such as special beam jammers, decoy beams, hyperdrives and extra missile racks for increased warhead payload. It was common for [[Alpha Squadron]], [[Avenger Squadron/Legends|Avenger Squadron]], [[Delta Squadron (TIE/D)/Legends|Delta Squadron]], [[Gamma Squadron/Legends|Gamma Squadron]], [[Sunspot Squadron]], and others to carry one or most of these pieces of special equipment at a time.<ref name="TSC" /><ref name="TIE Fighter: The Official Strategy Guide">''[[TIE Fighter: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref><ref name="Balance of Power in the Airam Sector">''[[Balance of Power in the Airam Sector]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Watch out, interceptors coming in.|A Rebel pilot during the Battle of Endor|<ref name="Rogue Squadron II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>}}
After the Empire's disastrous loss of 286 TIE/LN starfighters to the [[Lightspeed Panthers]] during the [[Fei Hu campaign]] in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the Empire realized the superiority of the Incom T-65 X-wing starfighters, and decided to create an interceptor model of the TIE series as a means to counter the X-wing, with development succeeding that same year.<ref name="EGW" /> In large part because of the success, they were later utilized in campaigns such as [[Operation Strike Fear]] and [[Operation Skyhook]].<ref name="X-wing">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> Interceptors however were also used in early Imperial conflicts, such as [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|putting down]] [[Gizor Dellso]]'s droid rebellion.<ref name="EGW" />

Another factor in its development was to have the power of the [[TIE/Advanced starfighter]] but be more cost-effective, as the TIE/Advanced was too expensive to mass-produce.

After the destruction of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Empire, realizing quickly the growing threat of the Rebel Alliance, increased mass production of the TIE Interceptors, thus resulting in the TIE Interceptors becoming the new fighter force of the Empire after the battle.
<div style="float:right">[[File:XWM_Imperial_Aces_box_cover.png|thumb|250px|A Royal Guard Interceptor flying alongside a 181st Interceptor.]]</div>
[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], aware of the superior abilities of the TIE Interceptor, as well as its relatively low cost, had planned to replace all standard TIE Fighters with Interceptors. By the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], TIE Interceptors filled twenty percent of the total Imperial starfighter complement, and overwhelmed many Rebel fighters.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" />

Two months following the defeat at Yavin, a squadron of Interceptors with concussion warhead mounts [[Mission to Dominus III|ambushed]] Rebel [[Scout/Legends|scouts]].<ref name="SW 1 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 1|''Star Wars'' (2013) 1]]</ref> Upgraded versions with shields and hyperdrives under the command of Colonel Bircher ambushed three members of [[Stealth Squadron|Gray Flight]]&mdash;[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and [[Tess Alder]].<ref name="SW 4 (DH)" /> Eleven of the Empire's starfighters were destroyed when the Gray Flight launched proton torpedoes at them. A member of Bircher's flight called for retreat, but the Colonel refused and gave the order for evasion pattern [[Delta Delta Victor]]. The Interceptors then broke off pursuit as their Star Destroyer prepared to fire.<ref name="SW 5 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 5|''Star Wars'' (2013) 5]]</ref>

The Rebels escaped<ref name="SW 5 (DH)" /> and the Imperials [[Ambush of Gray Flight|tracked]] them to their next rendezvous. Bircher once again led them into combat. More of his interceptors were destroyed by a Rebel trap, forcing Bircher to activate his craft's hyperdrive and go to rendezvous coordinates Beta One.<ref name="SW 6 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 6|''Star Wars'' (2013) 6]]</ref>

Soon after, Bircher led the ''Devastator'' to the Rebel fleet. He ordered all of his fighters to launch and [[Attack on the Rebel Fleet|destroy]] the fleet, and two interceptors were commandeered by the Rebel agents Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles, who had infiltrated the ship.<ref name="SW 10 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 10|''Star Wars'' (2013) 10]]</ref> The pair activated their afterburners and crash-landed aboard the flagship [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']]. Later, as the Rebels fought his fighters, he slaved external control to the cruiser and landed in Hangar Five.<ref name="SW 11 (DH)" />

TIE interceptors dueled with the Rebel's premier [[T-65B X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65B X-wing starfighter]] squadron, the [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogues]], in numerous battles<ref name="SW:RS">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> around six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the destruction of the Imperial Death Star.<ref name="RS I guide" /> A TIE Interceptor captured at the [[Liberation of Gerrard V]] was stored in the Rogue's hangar.<ref name="SW:RS" />

[[File:TIEinterceptor_bf.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A TIE Interceptor.]]
The TIE Interceptor was considered one of the best, if not the best starfighters for [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighting]]. It was often used by elite Imperial TIE squadrons like the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st]],<ref name="RS: Empire's Service">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: In the Empire's Service]]''</ref> the [[128th TIE Interceptor Squadron|128th]],<ref name="RS I guide" /> [[Alpha Squadron]], and [[Avenger Squadron/Legends|Avenger Squadron]]. The Interceptor was also used by squadron leaders in TIE/LN starfighter squadrons, as well as being used by Imperial personnel not in the Imperial TIE Fighter Corps, or the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels" /><ref name="Star Wars: Tie Fighter" /><ref name="SW:XvTF" />

Officers of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] were sometimes known to adopt TIE Interceptors as their personal craft, installing shield projectors and hyperdrives so the Interceptors could be utilized as escape vehicles. [[Apwar Trigit]] was one such officer.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" />

Modified TIE Interceptors were used by Warlord [[Zsinj]] in an attempt to bait and kill [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]. Finding that [[Wraith Squadron]] and [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], under Antilles' leadership, were significant impediments to his plans, the Warlord modified twelve Interceptors with droid brains and high-explosives. These ships would fly under the coordination of a central computer and be paired with a piloted craft. They were intended to close with enemy craft and detonate their explosive payloads. The two squadrons thus formed pretended to be the Imperial 181st Fighter Squadron under the command of [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Baron Soontir Fel]].<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" />

The Warlord knew that Antilles and Fel had a personal relationship, though he was unaware of its true nature. Using actors such as [[Tetran Cowall]] and computer voice modification, he was successful in his efforts to deceive Antilles. However, Voort saBinring deduced that the ships must be automated and jammed their signal, making them easy prey for the Wraiths and Rogues combined. Finally, Wedge splashed Fel's ship, only to discover Tetran Cowall instead of the Baron.<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" />

Due to limited pilots and fighters, [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] had many TIE Interceptors fitted with shields to minimize casualties during the reign of his [[Thrawn's confederation|Empire]]. This practice was continued after his death as the Empire could no longer afford to field profuse fleets of TIE Fighters.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|starship|tieinterceptor|TIE interceptor}}</ref>

Approximately [[15 ABY/Legends|eleven years after]] the Battle of Endor,<ref name="ImpWar">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref> TIE interceptors were considered an old craft and an unusual sight by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="Tales19">{{Tales|19|Collapsing New Empires}}</ref>

The TIE/IN starfighter later became the basis of the [[Predator-class fighter|''Predator''-class fighter]].<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 2006 0">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:TIEint_schem.jpg|thumb|right|180px|TIE Interceptor [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
Several sources state that the TIE/IN was the main reason behind the development of the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] by the Rebel Alliance (as a countermeasure) and that the Interceptor was deployed ''after'' Yavin.

However, the existence of the TIE Interceptor around the Battle of Yavin was well established in the timeline. Interceptors made appearances in [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' video game]], ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'', ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' (though the Lego Star Wars games are non-canon), and ''[[Star Wars: Lethal Alliance]]'', all of which take place before, during, or shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. [[West End Games]] ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' stated that at the time of Yavin, standard [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] carried one squadron of Interceptors (12 craft), one Bomber squadron, and four TIE/LN starfighter squadrons. By the time of the Battle of Endor, an additional Interceptor squadron has replaced that of the TIE/LN.

Numerous sources depict the TIE Interceptor as having only four wingtip cannons, but their ''very first'' appearance, in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], shows them firing their chin-mounted fifth and sixth cannons, in addition to their wingtip cannons throughout the Battle of Endor. It has since been established that each TIE Interceptor comes equipped with cannon mountings on the chin, like the preceding TIE Fighter, allowing for the addition of two more cannons.

In [[1998]], players could fly the Interceptor in unlocked missions in the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] if they earned all silver medals during the campaign.

The post-production speed/maneuverability chart for ''Return of the Jedi'' lists the TIE Interceptor as being able to go up to 125 MGLTs and having a maneuverability rating of High.<ref name="ROTJS">''[[Return of the Jedi Sketchbook]]''</ref>

Many of the models of the TIE Interceptor used in ''Return of the Jedi'' have four laser cannons on their wingtips; however, the main model used in the "''Return of the Jedi'' collection" section of the Blu-ray special edition only has two laser cannons total, on the top two wingtips. That may be due to the fragility of the model kit parts used to create the cannons, as publicity photos taken around the time of Return of the Jedi show the miniatures with four wingtip cannons.

===Contradictions===
Despite [[1989]]'s [[Starfighter Battle Book: X-wing vs TIE Interceptor]] listing the TIE/In's weaponry as four identical [[Senko Systems]] [[80-100 laser cannon|80-100 laser cannons]] with a fire control system which allowed only diagonally opposite guns to fire at the same time to facilitate rapid heat dissipation, in [[1994]] [[The Stele Chronicles]] booklet listed the craft's cannons as being [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|SFS]] [[L-s9.3 laser cannon/Legends|L-s9.3 laser cannons]] with no particular restictions of fire.
